books.title: What Happened After the Cross?
books.subtitle: A Mission Through Acts
books.description:
The apostles watched Jesus rise into a cloud. Days later a mighty rushing wind filled the Upper Room, tongues of fire rested on each of them, and the church was born. From that day one question followed the gospel from city to city: "How then were you baptized?"

This book walks through every baptism account in Acts, from Jerusalem to Samaria, the desert road, Damascus, Cornelius's house, a Philippian jail, Corinth, and Ephesus. Each chapter tells the story, sets out the Scripture, and adds historical context. Together they show one apostolic pattern of the new birth: repent, be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ, and receive the Holy Ghost, as believers did when they spoke in tongues. If you have ever wondered whether your baptism matches the Bible, this book asks you, "in the most loving way possible."

books.title: Conquering Leviathan
books.description:
Elior has done everything right. His fields rise in straight rows, his fences stand true, and he prays each morning. Then the small losses begin. A delivery never comes. A fence gives way. Some of the animals fall sick. Elior tightens his discipline and keeps standing, until his wife Mara tells him the hardest thing she can: “Not wait. Lean.”

This is a story for believers who are faithful and tired. Through Elior’s household and three trusted men who counsel him to endure, it exposes a quiet enemy: “pride disguised as faithfulness, control mistaken for obedience, fear dressed as righteousness.” Reflection questions and case studies from Saul, Jeroboam, Absalom, and David help you ask whether your faith is something you perform or something you receive.

books.title: Seven Altars Can’t Buy One Word from God
books.description:
Smoke rises from seven altars on a mountain in Moab. A frightened king has sent for a prophet to curse Israel, and he has done everything his religion told him to do. Then Balaam opens his mouth, and only blessing comes out. "I cannot reverse it."

This book walks slowly through Numbers 22 and 23, one mountain at a time. Each chapter sets the Scripture beside its historical setting, retells the scene, and shows where Christ is revealed in it. Along the way it exposes an old habit of the heart: trying to move God with effort, ritual, and a change of scenery. God had already spoken, and His Word does not change. From Moab the book points ahead to the cross and the Upper Room, where a humble people waited in obedient faith and heaven came down.

books.title: A Vision of the Harvest
books.description:
A drummer stays seated after a church service in Fort Worth and looks out over the congregation. In his mind's eye the people become a field. Some stalks stand full and ready. Some are stunted. Some are wilting. All of them remain under God's care.

That vision became this 52-week devotional. Each week opens with an ordinary moment from daily life, then turns to the Word, a prayer to pray together, and a family action step for the kitchen table. Over four quarters you learn to see the harvest, walk by faith, do the work, and pass faith on at home. It is written for believers and families who want evangelism to become "a way of life," lived out in hospitals and nursing homes, living rooms and lunch tables, wherever the Lord sends them.

books.title: Position and Placement
books.description:
Ephraim stands at the foot of a steep mountain trail, holding a note from his mentor Silas: “He is going to lead you to it so He can lead you through it.” Every believer comes to a trail like that. The valley is comfortable, but God is calling higher.

This book teaches that your position in God, and how well you understand it, determines your placement in His will. Starting from Hebrews 6 and working through Romans 1 to 8, it walks with Joseph, Moses, David, Esther, and King Uzziah to show that position always comes before placement. It lays out the new birth of repentance, baptism in Jesus’ Name, and receiving the Holy Ghost. It asks whether what we do is done in faith, and it calls you past the first principles into the work God prepared you for.

books.title: Untimely
books.description:
Three weeks after a joyful family wedding, the news came at 2:30 in the morning. A drunk driver had taken the lives of Loren and her best friend. In the stillness that followed, her father heard something in his spirit: "What feels so untimely to us is not untimely to God."

This is his testimony of the year that followed. Sit with him in a hospital room where a nurse says she treated the driver that night. Watch forgiveness grow from words spoken before they were felt. See a grief group become holy ground, an unfinished desk become a sermon, and a vision of a shattered vase come true. If your heart is broken, this book makes room for your tears, reminds you that God never wastes the pieces, and calls you to keep running this race.

books.title: When God Draws a Line in the Sand
books.subtitle: Reflections on Exodus and God’s Unfailing Promises
books.description:
Jesus knelt and wrote in the dust while a woman’s accusers stood over her. Long before that, at the edge of the Red Sea, God drew another line. Israel crossed on dry ground, and the same path became a trap for Egypt’s army. When God draws a line, it protects His people and it moves them forward.

Rooted in Exodus and reaching across all of Scripture, these eleven chapters set God’s covenant beside human promises that fade. They weigh Pharaoh’s shallow apologies against true repentance, sudden miracles against slow processes, and pride against humility. If you are standing at your own sea, tired and tempted to look back toward Egypt, this book says plainly that there is no “Plan B” with God. His covenant still stands, and His way still opens.

books.title: A Prophet’s Tale
books.description:
How does one king's fear become a nation's culture? This book traces rebellion from Jeroboam's golden calves, through Omri's Samaria and the Baal worship of Ahab and Jezebel, to a woman drawing water at noon. When she told Jesus, "Our fathers worshiped in this mountain," she was speaking from centuries of choices made before she was born.

This unified manuscript brings together two teachings also published on their own, Be Careful of the One You Put to Flight and Broken at the Well. It shows how sin born in weakness differs from sin born in rebellion, how one conversation with Jesus broke a generational shadow, and how Samaria received the Holy Ghost in Acts 8. "What one generation excuses, the next embraces, and the next defends as sacred." Weigh what your own choices are setting in motion.

books.title: When the Lines Grow Gray
books.description:
Picture two farms with a fence between them. One post leans and nobody fixes it. A generation later, children look across the land and ask if there was ever a boundary there at all. "The boundary did not move. Neglect made it difficult to see."

This teaching opens Ezekiel 22, where the priests "put no difference between the holy and profane," and follows Judah's compromise to broken walls and a burned Temple. Then it comes home. Under the New Covenant, God writes His law on the heart through the new birth and the indwelling Holy Ghost. You will learn to tell conviction from condemnation and to let truth examine your own heart first. Eight questions and a seven-day practice help you walk the rows of your own field. "We are called to be priests, not policemen."

books.title: When the Lines Grow Gray — Companion Study Workbook
books.description:
A fence line between two farms rarely falls all at once. A post leans, a wire breaks, the weeds grow in, and a new generation inherits a confusion it did not create. "The boundary did not move. Neglect made it difficult to see."

This companion workbook takes students and classes through the When the Lines Grow Gray lesson in twelve units, from Ezekiel 22:26 and Leviticus 10 to Romans 6, Galatians 2, James 2, and Hebrews 5:14. Inside are guided notes, word banks, fill-in-the-blank exercises, Scripture observations, short answers, and personal application, with a teacher's answer key in the back. It helps believers tell the holy from the common, conviction from condemnation, and grace-led obedience from self-will, and it closes with seven days of personal practice.

books.title: Broken at the Well
books.description:
Jews avoided Samaria at all costs. Jesus "must needs go through" it. To Jacob's well came a woman who had lost her identity, living in a region shaped by centuries of rebellion that began with Jeroboam's golden calves and grew under Omri and Ahab.

This teaching opens that history with help from Josephus, then shows what Jesus did with one conversation. He revealed Himself plainly to a woman who came to the well to hide. "Her shame became her sermon." The seeds planted that day bloomed in Acts 8, when Philip preached, baptisms multiplied, the Holy Ghost fell, and Peter and John laid hands on the believers. If your family history or your own past feels too broken to mend, this lesson brings a word from Samaria: "If He broke Samaria's curse… He can break yours."

books.title: Lord, Teach Me to Pray
books.description:
What do you do when the hunger is still there but the prayers are gone? After nearly 30 years of walking with God, the author came to that very place. He had hunger, yet "the prayer life was sucked out of me." The Lord met him there, and this message was born from that moment.

Jesus gave His disciples a structure for prayer. These ten short chapters walk through the Lord's Prayer phrase by phrase: relationship, worship, authority, surrender, provision, grace, mercy, guidance, deliverance, and glory. Each pairs Scripture with reflection and spoken declarations. You will pray for laborers in the harvest, learn to forgive, take up the weapons of spiritual warfare, and yield to the Spirit as He prays through you. "Prayer without faith is just noise." Journal prompts at the end help you answer God on paper.

books.title: A Prayer Journal
books.description:
"Many believers don't struggle with sincerity in prayer; they struggle with strategy." They have the desire. What they need is direction. This journal was compiled to help with exactly that.

Inside are Scripture-rooted prayers and declarations under plain headings: humility, making your home a house of prayer, breaking the spirit of pride, new identity, the spirit of infirmity, faith, boldness and courage, healing and health, purity, restoration, renewing the mind, and thanksgiving. You will also find the Lord's Prayer laid out by subject, ten Scriptures on God's mercy with reflection questions, and a call-and-response declaration for leading a group. Use a few in daily devotions, or pray through them all. Ten journal prompts and lined pages close the book, so you can pray "not as beggars, but as sons and daughters."

books.title: The Lord’s Prayer — Study and Devotional Journal
books.description:
Jesus gave His disciples a prayer that fits in a few lines. Every line opens a door: "Our Father in heaven," "Give us this day our daily bread," "As we forgive our debtors."

This short study handout breaks the Lord's Prayer into ten subjects: relationship with God, worship, His kingdom, His will, daily dependence, confession, forgiving others, guidance, deliverance, and God's glory. Each subject gives the line of Scripture with a few brief notes. A devotional journal follows with ten reflection questions, one for each subject, such as "Who do I need to forgive or release?" and "What do I need to trust God for today?" Use it in your own prayer time or with a study group, and let each line of the prayer become your own conversation with God.

books.title: Learning to Trust Again
books.description:
"Anxiety isn't always a lack of faith… sometimes it's the scar tissue of broken trust." Jesus pointed to the birds of the air. Not one of them has a job, a savings account, or a backup plan, and God feeds them every day. So why is the one made in His image the only thing in creation losing sleep?

Rooted in Matthew 6 and the Psalms, this message speaks to people who were hurt into anxiety. When trust has been wounded, concern sounds like criticism and silence feels like abandonment. Here you will find simple handles for rebuilding trust: pause before reacting, name the feeling, ask what else it could mean, and choose a better interpretation. It closes with a promise: "If God can be trusted to feed the world… He can be trusted with your life."

books.title: Marriage and Communication
books.description:
When did the two of you last talk honestly about money? About time, the children, your relatives, or how you would want to be comforted if tragedy came? Conversations like these shape a marriage whether we have them or not.

This study workbook gives couples a place to begin. Thirteen short chapters cover money, time, the sexual relationship, work, health, your relationship, the atmosphere in your home, children, relatives, God and church, death, friends, and outside activities. Each chapter opens with a verse of Scripture, then offers simple conversation starters, a practical suggestion for each one, a shared exercise, and lines for notes. It is built to be worked through together as a couple, one honest conversation at a time.

books.title: Still Speaking
books.subtitle: A Theological Rebuttal Against the Cessationist Misreading of Pentecost
books.description:
“The Holy Spirit has not retired.” Some teachers would put the tongues and prophecy of the Book of Acts in a museum of early church history. This booklet answers them from the Bible.

Still Speaking is a short theological rebuttal to cessationist teaching. It follows the pattern of Acts through Jerusalem, Samaria, Caesarea, and Ephesus: faith, repentance, water baptism, and Spirit baptism with the sign of tongues. It stands on the promise of Acts 2:39, given “to all that are afar off,” and on Paul’s words, “Forbid not to speak with tongues.” If the Spirit has not changed, neither has the way He moves. In the booklet’s own words, Pentecost is “a river flowing from the throne of God,” and it is still reaching whosoever will.

books.title: The Sword, the Sickle, and the Shield
books.description:
"I have put a sickle and a sword in your hand and a shield upon your arm." This teaching opens with a word of the Lord for the church. What has God placed in your hands, and what will you do with it?

Each tool is opened from Scripture. The sword is the Word of God and spiritual warfare, the blade Jesus used when He answered, "It is written." The sickle is harvest and holiness, reaping souls and discerning the holy from the unholy. The shield is faith that quenches every fiery dart. Then comes a charge: get connected, stand in the gap, and find your place in the field. The discipline of the special forces warrior and the obedience of the faithful soldier show what a laborer looks like. "It's time to get out of neutral."

books.title: The Bloom in the Battle
books.description:
The fire lily of South Africa needs fire to bloom. The desert rose stores water in its trunk and flowers on barren ground. Edelweiss grows on cold, high cliffs “where fear would freeze most out.” God plants His people in hard places too.

Drawn from Isaiah 35, where “the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose,” this message is for anyone walking through a dry season. It preaches three points: pressure produces power, pain produces praise, and persistence produces promotion. With Joseph in prison, David in the cave, and Paul and Silas singing in prison, it strengthens weak hands and confirms feeble knees. Its charge is plain: “If God planted you there, He intends for you to bloom anyway.”

books.title: Three Mantles
books.description:
What will your children one day put on because you wore it first? This Father’s Day message points to Elijah’s mantle as his glory, and to Ezra and Job tearing theirs in repentance and grief. It names three mantles God places on men and women: son or daughter, father or mother, patriarch or matriarch.

It starts where every mantle must start, with the new birth: repent, receive the Holy Ghost and speak in tongues, and be baptized in Jesus’ name for the remission of sins. Parents pass on a love for the Word, the truth that the Lord our God is one, and how to pray. Through Lois and Eunice it warns that the next generation “cannot be forged in a fire if it is not burning already in the generation leading them.”

books.title: How Were You Baptized? — For Kids
books.description:
What did Jesus tell His disciples to do before He went back to heaven? Ben heard the answer in Sunday school and felt "a fire in his heart." Before long he was telling his best friend Anna about it at the park.

This Pentecostal Bible lesson teaches children the Great Commission, baptism in Jesus' name, and receiving the Holy Ghost with the evidence of speaking in tongues. Younger children follow the story of Ben and Anna, with illustration ideas, a memory verse from Acts 1:8, and a prayer. Older children get a lesson plan built on Matthew 28:18-20 and Acts 2:38, discussion questions with answers, a "Power to Witness" megaphone game, and a closing challenge. It is a ready-to-teach draft for Sunday school teachers, children's church workers, and parents.

books.title: Source and Supply
books.description:
Are you worn out because the trial is too heavy, or because you have been trying to be the source? Paul heard the Lord say: "My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness." This Sunday school lesson starts at the cross, where Jesus defeated death, hell, and the grave, then asks why so many believers still run dry.

You will see how Job, Moses, Isaiah, Paul, Peter, and Gideon each found that weakness exposes the true source, and how Jesus, as the Son manifest in flesh, lived in complete dependence on the Father. You will follow the early church in Acts as the Holy Ghost directed, sent, and forbade them. "God never designed you to be the generator. He designed you to be connected." Stay connected to Him, and the supply never runs dry.

books.title: The Blessings in Brokenness
books.description:
Poor in spirit. Those that mourn. Hungry and thirsty for righteousness. Jesus called them blessed, and every one of them shares a mark: brokenness. The breaking of our will to embrace His. "The blessings are in brokenness."

This sermon teaching walks with people who knew what it was to be broken: Paul in the storm of Acts 27, Joseph lied on and imprisoned, David running from Saul, Hezekiah trembling before the king of Assyria, and Jesus Himself, broken and raised on the third day. It shows how God prunes, restores, and puts shattered pieces back together in His own hands. When you get the Holy Ghost, the commandments become "promises written in your heart." You do not have to be defined by what life has dealt you. You can be defined by what Jesus did on Calvary.

books.title: Be Careful of the One You Put to Flight
books.description:
We love to shout that one can chase a thousand and two put ten thousand to flight. Read Deuteronomy 32:30 in its setting, though, and it is a sobering word about a people routed by their enemies. The promise holds only when the Rock is with them. The same principle that multiplies faith can multiply rebellion.

This teaching follows that principle from David's fall and Solomon's divided heart, through the kings of Samaria who "walked in the sins of Jeroboam," to Acts 8, where Peter and John confirmed the revival with the Holy Ghost. Then it turns to you. As part of God's royal priesthood, your choices shape the ones who come after you, and the person you push away may be the one God sent to fight beside you. "Hell doesn't tremble at numbers; it trembles at covenant."

books.title: A Letter to the Girl I Used to Be
books.author: Grace Stacks
books.description: Grace Stacks writes to her younger self: the girl who felt things deeply, doubted her worth and her faith, and carried more than she could explain. It is for anyone learning who they are while carrying a story heavier than they expected, and a reminder that what shaped you never disqualified you from being loved or heard.

books.title: Grace’s Devotional
books.subtitle: Scripture, prayers, and notes of faith
books.author: Grace Stacks
books.description:
Some of the truest words about faith are written in pencil. Grace’s Devotional is Grace Stacks’ own notebook of walking with Jesus through everyday life, kept page by page with hand-lettered headings, colored-pencil hearts, drawings, and the Scriptures that carried her.

Inside are forty-nine short entries on the things young believers really face: friendship and gossip, social media, overthinking, comparing yourself, regrets, worry, and waiting on God. Each pairs a verse with her own reflection or prayer, like the reminder that “God isn’t delaying you. God is preparing you.” Read slowly. Keep your Bible nearby. Leave room to pray.

songs.title: From Trouble to Testimony
songs.description: A declaration of faith formed through pressure and waiting, tracing the road from struggle to a testimony of what God has done.

songs.title: Higher Ground
songs.description: When the storms of life close in, an unshakable anchor holds. Higher Ground lifts the eyes toward the mercy of Jesus and the promise of seeing Him face to face.

songs.title: We Will Overcome
songs.description: A bold gospel declaration of overcoming faith through the blood of the Lamb, giving the church words of courage, testimony, and praise.

songs.title: Still I Rise
songs.description: A declaration of faith that survives fire, flood, and the darkest night. With grace holding on through every scar, the song rises toward victory in Jesus’ name and the hope of heaven.

songs.title: Living by Faith
songs.description: A declaration of trust beyond what the eyes can see. Through trials and uncertain days, the hand of the Lord remains steady and His promises give reason to keep walking.

songs.title: A Beautiful Redemption
songs.description: A testimony of brokenness met by grace, celebrating the hope and restoration found in Jesus.

songs.title: More Than Conquerors
songs.description: Rooted in Romans 8, this song declares victory through the love of Christ and the assurance that nothing can separate His people from Him.

songs.title: Let the Redeemed Say So
songs.description: Drawing on Psalm 107, this song gives voice to people brought out of wandering, bondage, sickness, and storms by the God who answers their cries.

songs.title: I’ve Been Redeemed
songs.description: A joyful testimony of sins washed away, life made new, and freedom through the blood of the Lamb, looking ahead to the promised land.

songs.title: I Am a Soldier
songs.description: A declaration of steadfast faith in the Lord’s army, grounded in His Word, redeemed by His blood, and determined to remain faithful.

songs.title: I’ve Got Too Much to Lose
songs.description: A determined declaration that the grace, forgiveness, and victories already received are too precious to abandon. The road continues forward in faith.

songs.title: Closer to Your Throne
songs.description: A prayer for the nearness of God above everything the world can offer, finding renewed faith and freedom from fear in His presence.

songs.title: Fallow Ground
songs.description: A prayer for God to break the hardened places of the heart, plant fresh faith, and bring life to ground that has waited through a difficult season.

songs.title: Picking Up the Pieces
songs.description: A testimony of shattered dreams met by restoring grace, finding that the broken pieces of a life can become the beginning of something new in God’s hands.

songs.title: Back Home
songs.description: After rejection and broken belonging, an open door becomes a picture of grace. Back Home tells of finding welcome, acceptance, and a place where your name is still known.

songs.title: Porch Light On
songs.description: A father’s love keeps the door open without demanding explanations. This country ballad offers forgiveness, belonging, and the quiet assurance that home is still waiting.

songs.title: Angels Wings
songs.description: A tender song of grief, remembrance, and the hope of reunion in heaven, written to bring comfort to hearts carrying loss.

songs.title: I Hope You’re There
songs.description: A heartfelt look toward heaven, the Savior, and a home beyond sorrow, carrying the hope that those we love will be there too.

songs.title: Sunrise
songs.description: A song of love and second chances, holding to the belief that every sunset makes room for a sunrise and that a life shared in love is worth believing in.

songs.title: Sounds Like Livin’
songs.description: A country song about love and the everyday moments that make life worth living.

songs.title: Keep On Walking
songs.description: A gritty encouragement to keep moving forward in faith, one step at a time, even when the road is hard.

songs.title: Just Being Dad to You
songs.description: A country song about the everyday moments of fatherhood, from a back-door invitation to play to running beside a first bike ride, and the discovery that while a father was lifting his child, the child was lifting him too.

songs.title: Lean on the Lord
songs.description: A call to trust God with everything, great or small. Built on the promise of strength renewed on eagles' wings, it rises to a testimony: “I leaned on the Lord, and He carried me through.”

songs.title: When All I Have Is You
